dt-example.title: Hash location (name matching)
dt-example.info:
To round off our examples of URL options, this example demonstrates the use of a hash to indicate the state to load, this time using the state name as the identifier to match. [As before](./searchName) this should be used with caution if you allow the end user to change the name of their states, since it could impact on existing bookmarks.
In this case `-init stateRestore.bookmark.src` is set to `#dt-` which tells StateRestore to look for a hash that starts with `dt-`. Anything else will be ignored.
Updating the example links, we now have:
* [Search - London](./hashName#dt-Search%20-%20London) * [Order - Position](./hashName#dt-Order%20-%20Position) * [Search and order](./hashName#dt-Search%20and%20order)
Again, click the links to reload the page with the selected state active.
Next: [No URL rewriting](./update).
